newsitem.title: UK: N.Electric urges CE to increase offer.
newsitem.headline: N.Electric urges CE to increase offer.

text.p: British regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Electric chairman David Morris urged predator CE Electric to "get their cheque book out" to pay more than the 630 pence per share on offer.
"They are an excellent company but they need to get their cheque book out if they are going to further this bid at all," he told a press conference.
Morris said CE Electric, which is 70 percent owned by CalEnergy of the U.S. was "clearly going to have to pay a great deal more than 630 pence per share" to win control.
CE Electric has already bought nearly 30 percent of Northern as the Rec's shares have languished, weighed by worries the UK government might block the bid.
Northern brought forward half year results on Friday showing pretax profits of 50.7 million stg, down from 58.7 million stg, and said full year profits would be over 112 million stg.
It said gearing would be cut to 95 percent at March 31, 1997 from previous forecasts of 175 percent.
Morris said the market, which marked Northern's shares down a penny by 1340 GMT to 589 pence, had yet to take the results and forecasts on board.
"We believe we deserve consideration for a re-rating," he said.
"CalEnergy will have to put a much more sensible number on the table," Morris said.
Northern has claimed that a figure of 700 pence was discussed before CE Electric launched the bid in October but the Americans have denied this.
In its forecasts on Friday, Northern suggested valuations for the company at 745 pence and 825 pence.
Morris said the company was prepared to have discussions "on the basis of more than 700 pence."
CE Electric described Northern's results as "lacklustre."
